A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Neural Concept Verifier work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification, soundness, shortcut-mitigation and ablation results on CLEVR-Hans3/7, CIFAR-100 and ImageNet-1k, including supplementary experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds COCOLogic evaluations, toy classification experiments, additional baseline comparisons, sensitivity analyses and computational measurements.

M1.justification: The frozen concept extractor, cooperative and adversarial provers, nonlinear verifier, alternating optimization and Merlin-only inference are retained. Appendix A.4 newly specifies the modified rejection-aware loss and continuous-to-discrete mask updates as implementation clarifications; it does not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: v3 adds COCOLogic, extending evaluation to compositional classification on natural images. Appendix B also introduces generated XOR and exact-counting tasks using perfect concept encodings. The original datasets and confounded/non-confounded CLEVR-Hans scenarios remain.

E2.justification: Table 1 replaces the CIFAR-100 and ImageNet black-box ResNet-18 comparator with ResNet-50 and adds nonlinear CBMs to the main comparison. The CLEVR nonlinear scores reuse v1's pretraining results. Appendix C.4 additionally evaluates DCR, reporting scores on CIFAR-100 and COCOLogic and an ImageNet training timeout.

E3.justification: The reported CIFAR black-box setup changes from 300-epoch ResNet-18 training to 100-epoch ResNet-50 training; ImageNet switches to direct evaluation of pretrained ResNet-50 without fine-tuning. New protocols include 5,000-sample toy datasets with 80/20 splits, DCR hyperparameter searches, controlled gamma sweeps, and balanced COCOLogic metrics in Table 4 and Figure 5.

E4.justification: v3 adds a gamma sweep testing the contribution of adversarial training, a perfect-concept experiment isolating linear-classifier limitations, an ImageNet explanation case study, and computational-cost analysis. Existing mask-size and selector-architecture ablations remain unchanged. CLEVR-Hans3 shortcut results are moved from v1 Table 6 into v3 Table 2, rather than newly added.

E5.justification: The existing 20-seed CLEVR and 10-seed natural-image mean-and-standard-deviation reporting is retained. The new gamma analysis separately specifies three seeds per setting and plots their means without uncertainty bars. This adds replication information for new experiments, without establishing additional runs for retained results.

E6.justification: v3 adds COCOLogic results, including NCV completeness of 75.42±3.21 and soundness of 97.87±0.47, plus DCR, toy-task, gamma-sweep and timing results. Original NCV benchmark scores, shortcut results and mask-size ablation values remain unchanged. Updated ResNet results concern replacement architectures and protocols, not same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Where v1 mainly invokes existing Merlin-Arthur guarantees informally, v3 Appendix A presents average-precision and mutual-information bounds, feature-correlation and adversary-strength assumptions, and a class-wise one-vs-rest instantiation in concept space. This substantially expands the formal treatment, while explicitly stating that no new theorems are proved.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's five contributions and conclusion retain the same central claims: scaling PVGs through concepts, sparse nonlinear interpretability, competitive predictive performance and shortcut mitigation. The added benchmarks and analyses primarily provide further support for these retained contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix A substantially qualifies verifiability: guarantees are conditional, non-causal, class-wise, and dependent on adversary strength; reported soundness does not certify arbitrary worst-case subsets. It explains why numerical precision/information certificates are not estimated. Appendix B also qualifies linear-classifier limitations through task-sufficient concepts, while Appendix E.4 interprets the new evidence for Morgana's importance.

D1.justification: v3 newly documents the rejection-aware loss, gradient flow through continuous masks and hard-mask verifier updates, DCR implementation and search settings, COCOLogic hyperparameters, and A100/A40 hardware with timing conventions. These substantially expand reproducibility information. Conversely, v1's explicit 300-epoch CIFAR/ImageNet verifier-pretraining budget is omitted from v3's corresponding description.

R1.justification: Section 2 replaces v1's assertion that CBM classifier components received little attention with substantive discussion of nonlinear, symbolic, memory-based and causal approaches, including Barbiero et al. and Debot et al. NCV is explicitly positioned as a complementary prover-verifier framework around concept predictors, materially revising its relationship to prior work.

P1.justification: The abstract, background, concept-extraction explanation and evaluation narrative undergo substantial rewriting. Section 4.1 consolidates four numbered setup subsections into paragraph headings, and the supplementary narrative is reorganized around theory, motivation, baselines and implementation. These changes extend beyond inserting new scientific results.

P2.justification: Table 1 becomes a full-width comparison with datasets grouped horizontally; v1's two shortcut tables are merged into v3 Table 2. Figure 3 is redesigned to include an ImageNet example, and new toy-task, DCR and timing tables and a gamma-sweep figure are added. Existing supplementary explanation and ablation displays are retained and relocated.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially addresses v1's limited comparative evidence and underspecified connection to formal guarantees. COCOLogic, nonlinear comparators and the controlled Morgana ablation strengthen support for the central claims, while Appendix A clarifies theoretical boundaries and training details. DCR's different concept-prediction pipeline limits that comparison, and the shortcut prose still overstates NCV's zero-clean CLEVR-Hans3 result. Nevertheless, the gains in evidential support and transparency are substantial.
